newsitem.title: USA: CME March lumber closes down limit on cash concern.
newsitem.headline: CME March lumber closes down limit on cash concern.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended down the daily limit of $10.00 per tbf in March as renewed concerns about the cash market and interest rates weighed heavily on the market and touched off sell stops, traders said.
March lumber closed limit down at $390.00 per tbf with other months $9.50 lower to $5.00 higher. May ended near limit down at $379.50, off $9.50 per tbf.

Futures tumbled for limit losses early when Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan's statements on the economy added to concern over slow cash trade. Short covering then developed before prices fell again late, traders said.
Renewed concern developed late over slow retail demand for wood and possible heavy deliveries against the March contract, they said.
"We are not getting as much demand as people thought we would this time of the year," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.

Schmaedick added that many wholesalers bought wood expecting some kind of squeeze due to the quota over Canadian exports to the U.S. But this did not materialize as there is still nearly 40 pct of the quarterly quota left to export and cash markets look ready to ease.

Traders also noted increasing delivery concerns and apparent technical weakness in the market. Deliveries against March can be made up to three weeks after March goes off the board on the 17th and would allow deliveries to take place as late as the first week of April, the start of Canada's new quota year.
Technically, futures look weak after penetrating the $392 level, basis March. This is the lowest price of the year and dates back to December 26, they added.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $414 per tbf, unchanged from last Friday and up $2 from last Wednesday.
